stories.headline: A man posted one angry TikTok about his home builder. It has now cost him more than a million dollars.
stories.what: In Melbourne, Singh Homes ended Gurvinderpal Singh's building contract on 12 Feb 2024 over payment and workmanship disputes. He posted a Punjabi-language TikTok attacking the builder; it reached about 220,000 views, mostly in Melbourne's Punjabi community, and spread on WhatsApp. A jury found it called the directors dodgy builders who neglected customers.
stories.twist: The builder told the court about 12 prospective customers walked away, and Singh kept the video up until around July 2025 despite repeated requests, earning aggravated damages. Damages: A$673,000 to the company and A$105,000 to each director, A$883,000 in total, with costs and interest expected to pass A$1 million.
stories.why: Everyone has wanted to post an angry review. This is what one cost.
stories.result: Reported via SmartCompany and law-firm notes: A$883,000 damages, total over A$1M expected. 12 lost customers is the builder's claim. Appeal outcome: reports conflict.
stories.dates: Contract ended 12 Feb 2024 · director awards 28 Oct 2026 · reported 5 Nov 2026
stories.note: Entertainment 7 · Narrative 7 · Business 9 · Evidence 7 · Freshness 8. Original video removed (~Jul 2025); footage not found. The customer posted; the business won.

stories.headline: A mayor's campaign crowd surrounded a dumpling shop for backing his rival. Then both sides turned its Google reviews into a battlefield.
stories.what: On 6 Nov 2026 Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an campaigned through Liaoning Night Market. At the dumpling shop 又一村, which had a poster for his opponent Puma Shen, legislator Wang Hung-wei led supporters chanting outside while customers and children were inside. The owners posted their account; Chiang apologised on 8 Nov, then asked why other shops had no problem.
stories.twist: A legislator urged five-star Google reviews; others flooded it with one-star reviews and bot-like accounts swamped its posts. The shop closed for a day on 7 Nov. Then strangers covered its shutter in sticky notes, it reopened, the owner joined the rival's motorcade with a thank-you sign, and a councillor from the mayor's own party queued to buy dumplings.
stories.why: A tiny shop's window poster became the centre of a city election.
stories.result: Reported via LTN, Yahoo TW, Mirror Media/SETN, Business Today: one-day closure, reopened. Revenue unknown. Bot accounts: unverified claim.
stories.dates: Incident 6 Nov 2026 · closure 7 Nov · apology 8 Nov · councillor visit 9 Nov
